assets.name: kotodama: fun, keep going with it (12)

status_from.text: Picked in review minigames-3: Kotodama picked: keep going (tap-only and better machines done in 246fd2df, 61ab7bce)

assets.source: The pitch: B2 after six, and the old machines do exactly what Eric says, word for word. You build each command from the room itself (tap who and what, give each a particle, then fire the verb), and the particles decide what flies where. Requests pile up faster than one command can answer them one at a time, so と (two or three people served in one sentence) is the combo you need, scored 2 × 2 or 3 × 3 with a streak on top. Between shifts you pick a power word: も, みんな, まって or ください. Three shifts, three hearts, a daily run with a best score. The design page, with what it borrows and an honest check, is game3d/minigames/README.md (Kotodama). The screens come from a headless run of the daily seed; the frame strips are from game3d/minigames/tools/frames.mjs. · Kotodama: a new grammar game from scratch

assets.name: kotodama: fun, keep going with it (2)

status_from.text: Picked in review minigames-3: Kotodama picked: keep going (tap-only and better machines done in 246fd2df, 61ab7bce)

assets.source: The pitch: B2 after six, and the old machines do exactly what Eric says, word for word. You build each command from the room itself (tap who and what, give each a particle, then fire the verb), and the particles decide what flies where. assets.source: What changed: each of the four rounds is a small puzzle. Everyone at the table gave one drink and got one, and sits with the one they got. People say what happened from their own side (the giver says あげました, the one who got it says くれました or もらいました, dropping わたし the way people do), and one person never says anything, so the last arrow has to be worked out. You draw all the arrows, then press Thank them: everyone thanks whoever your drawing says gave them theirs. A wrong arrow sends a thank-you to the wrong person, who reacts (Kenji takes the credit), and Mio points at the line that gave it away. Run counter, ticks and crosses on whoever was thanked, two endings depending on how many thank-yous went wrong, and two rounds end with Eric saying his own hand-over. 15 arrows, 38 steps on a clean run instead of 44, no timers, English shown in round 1 and one tap away after. Screens are from a headless run that got every third arrow wrong on purpose, so the mix-ups show; the last three are desktop. · Friday drinks: the giving game, made into a puzzle

assets.name: friday-drinks: the new giving game (give.html)

status_from.text: Not picked in review minigames-2 (superseded): even less fun, start over, write a new game from scratch, make it the most fun and impressive grammar game in existence

assets.source: What changed: each of the four rounds is a small puzzle. Everyone at the table gave one drink and got one, and sits with the one they got. People say what happened from their own side (the giver says あげました, the one who got it says くれました or もらいました, dropping わたし the way people do), and one person never says anything, so the last arrow has to be worked out. You draw all the arrows, then press Thank them: everyone thanks whoever your drawing says gave them theirs. A wrong arrow sends a thank-you to the wrong person, who reacts (Kenji takes the credit), and Mio points at the line that gave it away. Run counter, ticks and crosses on whoever was thanked, two endings depending on how many thank-yous went wrong, and two rounds end with Eric saying his own hand-over. 15 arrows, 38 steps on a clean run instead of 44, no timers, English shown in round 1 and one tap away after. Screens are from a headless run that got every third arrow wrong on purpose, so the mix-ups show; the last three are desktop. · Friday drinks: the giving game, made into a puzzle
